questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) while the employees

(B) meeting on time

(C) the boss arrived at the

(D) despite the heavy traffic

(E) were late
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (1)** i.e. **DCBAE**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence logically starts with the phrase that sets the context of the situation, which is part (D) "despite the heavy traffic."
 
• Next follows part (C) "the boss arrived at the," which continues the main clause.
 
• Then part (B) "meeting on time," completes the main clause describing the boss's punctuality.
 
• Part (A) "while the employees," adds a subordinate clause introducing a comparison group affected by the situation.
 
• Finally, part (E) "were late," completes the sentence by specifying the state of the employees.

Therefore, the correct answer is **DCBAE**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2 (DACEB):** This option places part A too early, disrupting the flow of the contextual information.
 
• **Option 3 (BACED):** This option starts with part B, which leads to a confusing sentence structure and disrupts logical sequencing.
 
• **Option 4 (ACEDB):** This option starts with part A, which disrupts the flow and logical order of the sentence.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Charles Darwin is renowned for his book on evolution, 'On the Origin of Species', which __laid down a treasure of substantiation __that evolution occurs, and projected a mechanism, that is, natural selection, for how it does so.

options.text: laid into a treasure of substantiation
laid about a treasure of substantiation
laid away a treasure of substantiation
laid out a treasure of substantiation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'D' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase 'laid down a treasure of substantiation' is incorrect. The correct phrasal verb to use in this context is 'laid out a treasure of substantiation'.
 
• The word **'laid out'** means to **explain or present something clearly. **
 
• This phrasal verb is appropriate because Darwin's book **presents** a well-explained and clear body of evidence for the theory of evolution.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *Charles Darwin is renowned for his book on evolution, 'On the Origin of Species', which **laid out a treasure of substantiation** that evolution occurs, and projected a mechanism, that is, natural selection, for how it does so.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When using phrasal verbs such as **'laid out'**, ensure they fit the context of the sentence for proper meaning.
 
• Each phrasal verb has a specific usage, and using them correctly enhances sentence clarity and coherence.

questions.question:

__

• The correct form should use 'works' since the relative pronoun 'who' refers to 'he,' which is a singular pronoun.

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The teachers of our school have already taken this training.

options.text: This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school.
This training has been taken by the teachers of our school.
This training has already been taken by the our school teachers.
This training was already taken by the teachers of our school.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "The teachers of our school have already taken this training."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "this training" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "have taken" to "has been taken" (present perfect passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "the teachers of our school."
 
• Ensure the time phrase "already" is positioned correctly in the sentence for clarity.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"This training has already been taken by the teachers of our school."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"This training has been taken by the teachers of our school." – This option is missing the word "already" and does not fully match the context of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3: **"This training has already been taken by the our school teachers." – This option contains a grammatical error ("the our school teachers").
 
• **Option 4: **"This training was already taken by the teachers of our school." – This option uses the wrong tense (past simple passive instead of present perfect passive).

questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

(A) he had to take the bus

(B) his friend, who used to give

(C) to his office because he had

(D) him a lift, was on vacation

(E) never learned to drive and
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** Option (2)** i.e. **ACEBD**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence logically starts with part (A) "he had to take the bus," which introduces the action taken by the subject.
 
• Next follows part (C) "to his office because he had," which provides the reason for the action in part (A).
 
• Then part (E) "never learned to drive and," offers additional information about the subject’s inability.
 
• Part (B) "his friend, who used to give," introduces the friend who used to assist him.
 
• Finally, part (D) "him a lift, was on vacation," completes the sentence by explaining why the assistance was unavailable.

Therefore, the correct answer is **ACEBD**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1 (DACEB):** This option disrupts the logical flow by starting with the reason for the action rather than the action itself.
 
• **Option 3 (EBADC):** This option disrupts the logical flow by starting with the subject’s inability rather than the action or reason.
 
• **Option 4 (BADEC):** This option disrupts the logical flow by starting with the subject’s friend rather than the action itself.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

Ravi will play the match.

options.text: The match is played by Ravi.
The match will have been played by Ravi.
The match will be playing by Ravi.
The match will be played by Ravi.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Passive voice structure: The object of the active voice sentence becomes the subject of the passive voice sentence.
 
• In the active voice, the sentence is: "Ravi will play the match."
 
• To convert to passive voice: Place the object "the match" at the beginning.
 
• Change the active verb form "will play" to "will be played" (future simple passive).
 
• Add the preposition "by" followed by the original subject "Ravi."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The match will be played by Ravi."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The match is played by Ravi." – This option uses the present simple passive instead of the future simple passive.
 
• **Option 2: **"The match will have been played by Ravi." – This option uses the future perfect passive, which is incorrect in this context.
 
• **Option 3: **"The match will be playing by Ravi." – This option is grammatically incorrect as it incorrectly uses the future continuous tense in passive form.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

questions.solution:

__
 
• In the fourth part of the given sentence, the adverb form 'violently' should be used instead of the adjective 'violent'.
 
• Adverbs modify verbs and are needed to correctly describe the action.
 
• Adjectives modify nouns and should not be used to describe verbs.
 
• Therefore, the adverb form 'violently' should be used instead of 'violent'.

Correct sentence: *The windows violently banged during the storm yesterday.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
